prerequisites: Differential equations resolution and Fourier and Laplace transform applications.
Fundamental elements of electrical engineering knowledge.
Fundamentals of automatic knowledge (Bode diagrams, Feedback).

learning_outcomes.text: Students will gain a deep understanding of the operating principles of basic electronic devices (diodes, MOSFETs, operational amplifiers) as well as the structure and operation of fundamental logic gates and integrated circuit families, both analog and digital.

Students will be able to analyze and size basic analog and digital electronic circuits, evaluate the frequency response of amplifiers, design basic block diagrams, and configure microcontroller- and sensor-based data acquisition systems.

Students will be able to critically evaluate the performance of an electronic circuit, select the most suitable circuit topology based on design specifications, and independently interpret experimental data measured during laboratory sessions.

Students will be able to present theoretical concepts of electronics clearly, rigorously, and with appropriate technical language, as well as write clear and concise technical reports regarding the experimental activities carried out in the laboratory.

Students will develop the capability to independently consult and interpret technical manuals (datasheets) of electronic devices and components, which is essential for the continuous updating of their practical skills.

syllabus_topics: Operational Amplifiers Ideal operational amplifier: definition, characteristics, inverting and non-inverting configurations
Current-voltage characteristic: forward, reverse, and breakdown regions
Rectifier circuits: single and double half-wave, bridge rectifier, Zener diodes, voltage regulators, precision half-wave rectifier (superdiode)
MOS Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) Structure and operation of enhancement and depletion MOSFETs
Current-voltage characteristics, circuit symbols, and graphical representations
Fundamental MOSFET amplifier configurations with resistive and active loads
Digital Circuits Introduction to digital electronics
Logic inverter as a binary element
Transfer characteristic of the logic inverter
Integrated Circuit Technologies Moore’s law and integration scales
Silicon in electronic and optical devices
Oxidation, deposition (CVD, PVD), lithography and photolithography (X-ray, electron beam)
MOS Transistor Structure of the MOS transistor
Capacitance and layout of the MOS device
NMOS Logic Gates NMOS inverter with resistive and active loads
Circuit capacitance, dynamic analysis, and propagation delays
CMOS Logic Gates CMOS inverter, transfer characteristics, and noise margins
Dynamic behavior, propagation delays, and power dissipation
Combinational circuits: NOR, NAND, XOR, adders, subtractors, comparators, encoders, decoders, multiplexers, and demultiplexers
Sequential and bistable circuits: SR bistable, synchronized, JK, Master-Slave, D-T flip-flops
Arduino Platform and Educational Laboratories Arduino platform for sensor nodes, data acquisition, and actuation in IoT
Experimental characterization and laboratory experiences: measurement instrumentation, inverting/non-inverting operational amplifiers, rectifiers with filters, and sensor/actuator management
assessment_rules: The assessment will be through an oral interview, evaluating knowledge, application ability, critical spirit, and clarity of exposure. The final grade, out of thirty, will be based on maturity in course contents, oral exposure quality, critical spirit, autonomy of judgment, and mastery of scientific language. The oral examination may include discussion of classroom exercises and laboratory projects, with the quality of the report and the student's knowledge and critical spirit influencing the final grade. Praise is awarded for an oral test that fully satisfies the evaluation criteria.
